sections.title: What in-house SEO provides
sections.body: An in-house team holds context close. It can build relationships with product, development and leadership, retain institutional knowledge and respond within existing processes. The trade-off is the time and management required to recruit, support and retain the capability.

sections.title: What white-label SEO provides
sections.body: A white-label partner adds bounded capacity or specialist judgement without making the agency build every role first. The benefit depends on the quality of the handoff, review route and communication boundary.

sections.title: Compare total operating effort
sections.body: Compare salary and employment overhead with partner scope, account time, quality review and client communication. Neither model has a universal cost advantage. The right comparison uses the work your agency actually needs.

sections.title: Keep review independent of production
sections.body: Whether work is internal or outsourced, recommendations need an owner who can challenge them. Evidence, assumptions and verification should remain visible. A white-label arrangement fails when the agency cannot inspect what it presents.

sections.title: Use a deliberate combination
sections.body: An agency may keep strategy and client ownership in-house while using a partner for audits, briefs, technical investigation or overflow. Define the boundary so the hybrid model does not create duplicate research or unclear accountability.

sections.title: Choose for the constraint you have
sections.body: Choose in-house when context, continuity and close collaboration dominate. Choose white-label support when demand is bounded, specialist or uneven. Revisit the choice when service scope, team capacity or client expectations change.

cta.title: Define the delivery boundary before adding capacity
